newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian unions plan protest at CRA AGM.
newsitem.headline: Australian unions plan protest at CRA AGM.

text.p: Workers and conservationists plan to protest against Anglo-Australian mining giant RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd's "anti-union tactics" and environmental record at its Australian annual meeting of shareholders on Wednesday.
The protest, to be coordinated by the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU), will begin as shareholders arrive for the meeting in Melbourne, the ACTU said in a statement.
Last year's annual meeting turned nasty when CRA coal-miners blocked the entrance to the meeting hall.
Hundreds of shareholders were abused by angry miners as they entered the building through a barricade of police officers.
One shareholder collapsed and was taken to hospital.
Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU) president John Maitland said on Tuesday unionists would adopt a quieter approach this year.
Some would use their status of shareholders to quiz the company's Australian board of directors on issues such as profit, possible asset sales and executive salaries, he said.
"On this occasion we are not planning a big protest," Maitland told Reuters.
"We are taking our argument directly to the directors and the shareholders," he said.
